document_summary: California Business and Professions Code section 16729 (AB 325), which bars use or distribution of a common pricing algorithm in restraint of trade; it applies statewide to all products and services, including rental housing.

rules.title: Common pricing algorithm prohibition (Cartwright Act, AB 325)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy in restraint of trade, or to coerce another person to adopt a price or commercial term the algorithm recommends.
rules.key_value: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm (competitor-data-based) to set prices or commercial terms in restraint of trade or through coercion
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person using or distributing a methodology (including software) used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. It is not limited to housing; it covers rental pricing as a product or service.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to end consumers of a product or service.
rules.interaction: Does not impair or limit the applicability of other antitrust laws. It is a statewide rule that applies alongside any local algorithmic rent-setting ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.extraction_notes: Added by Stats. 2025, Ch. 338, Sec. 1 (AB 325), effective January 1, 2026, per the history note. The text is general antitrust law and does not mention rent or housing expressly; it is included because a common pricing algorithm can cover rent-setting software.
